chapter.heading: Preparations for Worship
chapter.v:
When David
was old, having lived a long life, he made his son Solomon king of Israel.

He also
summoned all the leaders of Israel, the priests, and the Levites.

The Levites
over thirty years old were counted, and there was 38,000 in total.

“Of these
24,000 will be in charge of the work of the house of the Lord, while 6,000 will be officers and judges,” David instructed.

“And 4,000
will be gatekeepers, while 4,000 will praise the Lord using the musical instruments I have provided for praise worship.”

David divided
them into sections corresponding to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

The sons
of Gershon: Ladan and Shimei.

The sons
of Ladan: Jehiel (chief), and Zetham, and Joel, three in total.

The sons
of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three in total. These were the leaders of the families of Ladan.

The sons
of Shimei: Jahath, Zizah, Jeush, and Beriah—four in total.

Jahath (chief),
and Zizah (second); but because Jeush and Beriah did not have many sons they were counted as a single family.

The sons
of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel—a total of four.

The sons
of Amram: Aaron and Moses. Aaron was dedicated to service with the most holy things, that he and his sons should always present offerings to the Lord, and minister before him, and give blessings in his name forever.

As for
Moses, the man of God, his sons were included with the tribe of Levi.

The sons
of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer.

The sons
of Gershom: Shebuel (chief).

The sons
of Eliezer: Rehabiah (chief). Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah had many sons.

The sons
of Izhar: Shelomith (chief).

The sons
of Hebron: Jeriah (chief), Amariah (second), Jahaziel (third), and Jekameam (fourth).

The sons
of Uzziel: Micah (chief) and Isshiah (second).

The sons
of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish.

Eleazar died
without having sons, only daughters. Their cousins, the sons of Kish, married them.

The sons
of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three in total.

These were
the descendants of Levi by family, the heads of families chiefs listed individually by name—those twenty years of age or more who served in the house of the Lord.

For David
said, “The Lord, the God of Israel, has given peace to his people, and he will live in Jerusalem forever.

So the
Levites don't need to carry the Tent any longer, or anything needed for its service.”

In accordance
with David's final instructions, Levites twenty years of age or more were counted.

Their assignment
was to help the descendants of Aaron with the service of the house of the Lord They were responsible for the courtyards and rooms, for cleansing all the holy things, and the work of the service of the house of God.

They were
also responsible for the showbread that was placed on the table, the special flour for the grain offerings, the unleavened bread, the baking, the mixing, and dealing with all amounts and measurements.

They also
had to stand every morning to give thanks and praise to the Lord, and do the same in the evening,

and whenever
burnt offerings were presented to the Lord whether on Sabbaths, new moons, and feast days. They were to serve regularly before the Lord according to the number required for them.

So the
Levites were to carry out the responsibility of caring for the Tent of Meeting and the sanctuary, and with their brothers the descendants of Aaron, they served the house of the Lord.
